text: Technology has transformed almost every part of modern society, from the way we work to the way we interact with friends and family. The widespread use of social media and smartphones has made instant connectivity possible, but it has also created new problems, such as people becoming addicted to their screens and finding it hard to disconnect. Meanwhile, breakthroughs in artificial intelligence are changing the workforce, as companies use algorithms to automate tasks that used to require human workers. This kind of innovation can increase efficiency and convenience, but it also raises questions about job security and privacy. Every time we go online, our personal data is collected, which has led to growing concerns about surveillance and cybersecurity. Although many people are dependent on digital devices for work, education, and entertainment, experts argue that we should not let technology control our lives completely. Instead, they suggest that society needs clear rules to protect personal information and ensure that new technology benefits everyone, not just large companies. As artificial intelligence continues to influence more areas of daily life, finding a healthy balance between embracing innovation and protecting our privacy will remain one of the biggest challenges of the twenty-first century.
